note.question: How do strategic timing and dynamic pricing interact for online resource allocation?
note.overview: This paper optimizes dynamic pricing and real-time resource allocation policies for a platform facing nontransferable capacity, stochastic demand-capacity imbalances, and strategic customers with heterogenous price and time sensitivities. We characterize the optimal mechanism, which specifies a dynamic menu of prices and allocations. Service timing and pricing are used strategically to: (i) dynamically manage demand-capacity imbalances, and (ii) provide discriminated service levels.

This paper optimizes dynamic pricing and real-time resource allocation policies for a platform facing nontransferable capacity, stochastic demand-capacity imbalances, and strategic customers with heterogenous price and time sensitivities.
A platform operates continuously over a discretized inﬁnite time horizon, and matches capacity with a demand of customers (“agents”).
The platform transfers strictly more n-type agents than required to serve all late demand.
Consider an on-demand platform (e.g., Uber, Lyft, TaskRabbit), a delivery company (e.g., UPS, FedEx, Rivigo, Amazon), and a cloud computing provider (e.g., Microsoft, Google, Amazon).
